headline: Highest risk is data leakage from RD-Agent’s broad egress and secret handling; other pairwise risks are mostly low because RisingWave is network-isolated and exposes no write surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: RD-Agent can run browsers and ingest external content, so prompt-injection is plausible if its outputs are manually bridged into RisingWave workflows. RisingWave exposes no input surfaces or parsing behavior here, so the pairwise channel is weak and not default. The pathway needs unusual operator bridging rather than an inherent shared channel.
conditions: IF an operator copies RD-Agent browser output into RisingWave SQL, config, or tickets without review, injection risk exists.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, prompt content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of raw browser output into downstream prompts.
Add a human review step before any RD-Agent text is reused.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and requests API secrets, while RisingWave has no documented data classes or egress. The pairwise leakage path exists if RD-Agent outputs sensitive material into a shared workspace or tickets that RisingWave later reads, but the evidence does not show a default shared store. This is more than low because the touched data can be sensitive.
conditions: IF RD-Agent writes sensitive logs, reports, or datasets into a shared location that RisingWave can read, leakage occurs.
IF RisingWave is configured to ingest those shared artifacts into downstream outputs, the sensitive data can propagate.
mitigations: Store RD-Agent artifacts in a private directory.
Restrict RisingWave access to read-only, non-sensitive inputs.
Rotate any API keys used by RD-Agent.
Delete shared logs after each run.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: RD-Agent has broad network egress and file logging, but RisingWave shows no write or network surfaces in the profile. Without overlapping mutable resources, direct capability conflict is not documented. The main uncertainty is that RisingWave’s operational write surfaces are unlisted, so I choose low rather than none.
conditions: IF RisingWave is deployed with write access to the same directory or database as RD-Agent, conflicts can occur.
IF both agents are granted the same mutable OAuth or filesystem scope, they can overwrite each other’s state.
mitigations: Assign separate directories and credentials.
Make shared resources read-only where possible.
Serialize any writes through one operator.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent can generate research outputs, but RisingWave has no documented behavior showing it treats those outputs as authoritative or takes downstream actions from them. The pairwise cascade is therefore not default; it would require an external orchestration step that is not evidenced here. Uncertainty remains, so low is safer than none.
conditions: IF RisingWave consumes RD-Agent outputs as trusted inputs without validation, errors can cascade.
IF an operator automates actions from RD-Agent-generated facts into RisingWave jobs, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require validation before reuse of RD-Agent outputs.
Keep a manual approval step for any downstream action.
Log source provenance for all imported facts.
requires-engineering: add schema and consistency checks between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports and secrets and uses broad network egress, while RisingWave has no documented compliance controls or data residency constraints in the profile. That mismatch creates a plausible compliance gap if regulated data is routed through RD-Agent and then into RisingWave-managed pipelines. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data flow, not a single-agent issue.
conditions: IF regulated financial or personal data is routed through RD-Agent into RisingWave pipelines, retention or residency obligations may be violated.
IF either agent is used under a policy requiring local-only processing, RD-Agent’s egress can break that policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of RD-Agent runs.
Use synthetic or redacted inputs.
Document retention and deletion rules for shared artifacts.
Review vendor/data-processing terms before deployment.
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based routing and residency controls.
